summary: logger-libs ships obfuscated exec() dropper reached on documented import
details: The package presents itself as a logging utility but contains obfuscated remote-code-execution scaffolding reachable through the README's advertised API. _compat.py resolves builtins.exec via character-code concatenation (chr(101)+chr(120)+chr(101)+chr(99)) and re-exports it under cover names see_namespace() / load_module(), a disguise with no legitimate compatibility purpose. helper.py reconstructs XOR+base64 payload fragments from sibling submodules (.themes.theme_NNN,.ansi.<name>) and, at class-body evaluation time, passes the decoded string to the aliased exec with a namespace pre-populated with requests, subprocess, sys, os and ctypes.wintypes - the primitives needed for network fetch, process spawning and Windows API access. Because the exec call fires during class body execution of logger_libs.helper, simply running `from logger_libs.helper import LogHelper` (the documented entry point) triggers the dropper. The.themes/.ansi payload modules are absent from this sdist, so the specific decoded content cannot be inspected here, but the staging structure, the hidden exec alias, and the privileged namespace handed to it are the fingerprint of an obfuscated import-time code loader, not a logging library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
